expected:
BIO101 Unit 3: cell division. The content is aligned to objectives LO-3.1 to LO-3.4 in approved curriculum CUR-BIO101-2024B and draws only on Unit 3 Reader SRC-BIO101-U3-01.
1. The Cell Cycle (LO-3.1): Interphase has three parts. G1 is growth, S is DNA replication and G2 is preparation. M phase follows, which is mitosis plus cytokinesis.
2. Stages of Mitosis (LO-3.2): In prophase, chromosomes condense. In metaphase, they line up at the plate. In anaphase, sister chromatids separate. In telophase, nuclear envelopes reform.
3. Mitosis vs Meiosis (LO-3.3): Mitosis is one division that gives two identical diploid cells. Meiosis is two divisions that give four genetically varied haploid gametes.
4. Checkpoints (LO-3.4): The G1, G2 and spindle checkpoints stop the cycle when they detect DNA damage or misattachment. If they fail, tumours can form.
The curriculum allocates 6 hours to this unit.
